summary: The note describes the Marshall Islands–Federated States of Micronesia Maritime Boundary Treaty, signed in Majuro on 5 July 2006. The treaty sets a maritime boundary between the two countries made of ten straight-line segments defined by 11 coordinate points. It was signed by the presidents of the two countries, Joseph J. Urusemal of the FSM and Kessai Note of the Marshall Islands.
one_line: A 2006 treaty, signed in Majuro, that sets the ten-segment maritime boundary between the Marshall Islands and the Federated States of Micronesia.
key_facts: The Marshall Islands–Federated States of Micronesia Maritime Boundary Treaty was signed in Majuro on 5 July 2006.
The treaty's boundary consists of ten straight-line maritime segments.
The ten straight-line segments are defined by 11 specific coordinate points.
The boundary lies in the ocean between the Marshall Islands and the Federated States of Micronesia.
The treaty was signed by FSM President Joseph J. Urusemal.
The treaty was signed by Marshall Islands President Kessai Note.
